words.gloss: those who attained the supreme state

parts.gloss: having been caught in a net

words.gloss: those who are caught in the net

literal: Those who attained the supreme state are those who renounced completely; being deluded, caught in the net are the other people.
translation: Those who have completely renounced all attachments have attained the supreme state of liberation; all others, remaining deluded, are caught in the net of worldly bondage.
modern: முற்றிலுமாகப் பற்றுகளைத் துறந்தவர்களே முக்தி நிலையை அடைந்தவர்கள் ஆவர்; அவ்வாறு துறக்காத மற்றவர்கள் மயக்கமுற்று உலக ஆசை என்னும் வலையில் சிக்கியவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts those who achieve spiritual liberation with those who remain bound to worldly existence. The term 'தலைப்பட்டார்' refers to those who have reached the highest state of spiritual attainment, which is achieved only by those who have renounced everything completely ('தீரத் துறந்தார்'). On the other hand, those who do not renounce ('மற்றையவர்') remain in a state of delusion ('மயங்கி'). This delusion causes them to be trapped like prey in a net ('வலைப்பட்டார்'), representing the inescapable snare of worldly desires and attachments.
